    "content": "Meta doubles down on AI with $21 billion CoreWeave (CRWV) partnership Search / News Video Prices Research Consensus 2026 Data & Indices Sponsored Search / en Markets Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email The $21 billion AI bet: Meta and CoreWeave ink deal for NVIDIA\u2019s next-gen superchips Long-term agreement between Meta and CoreWeave signals growing demand for scalable AI compute and inference capacity. By James Van Straten , AI Boost | Edited by Jamie Crawley Apr 9, 2026, 12:19 p.m. Make preferred on Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg (Shutterstock) What to know : Meta locks in AI cloud capacity through 2032 to support ongoing AI deployment. CoreWeave strengthens its position in the fast-growing AI infrastructure market. CRWV shares rise 3% pre-market. CoreWeave (CRWV) and Meta (META) have broadened their existing partnership, originally valued at up to $14.2 billion , with a new agreement worth around $21 billion . As part of the deal, CoreWeave will supply dedicated cloud capacity to Meta through 2032, helping power the development and rollout of its AI technologies. The infrastructure will span multiple locations and feature early deployments of NVIDIA\u2019s (NVDA) Vera Rubin platform, aimed at boosting efficiency, reliability, and scale. The NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform is the next-generation AI supercomputing architecture is expected to mark a massive shift from simple \"Generative AI\" to \"Agentic AI,\" whereby AI becomes more proactive in executing steps towards its goals rather than relying on human prompts. A key focus of the CoreWeave-Meta agreement is inference, reflecting the industry\u2019s shift toward running AI systems continuously rather than just training them. \u201cThis is another example that leading companies are choosing CoreWeave\u2019s AI cloud to run their most demanding workloads,\u201d said CEO Michael Intrator. The deal signals that large tech companies are increasingly securing long-term compute resources to support AI-driven services. Shares of CoreWeave rose 3% in pre-market trading on Thursday.     "content": "Not Crazy to Go Long CoreWeave After Meta Commits Another $21 Billion | TheStreet Pro Pro Insights = Smarter Trades Go Pro Now Subscribe HOME PORTFOLIO LATEST AUTHORS DAILY DIARY COLUMNS THESTREET.COM LATEST Home Technical Analysis Trade Ideas Market Commentary Investing Dividends Options Short Selling Earnings Home > trade-ideas trade-ideas Not Crazy to Go Long CoreWeave After Meta Commits Another $21 Billion How to make an investment in the AI cloud infrastructure firm after a pair of significant announcements. Stephen Guilfoyle \u00b7 Apr 9, 2026, 11:05 AM EDT You're reading 0 of 1 free page. Register to read more or Unlock Pro \u2014 50% Off Ends Soon Register Not logged in? Click here to log in Coreweave CoreWeave ( CRWV ) is in the news on Thursday morning. They sure are. A new agreement was announced between CoreWeave and Meta Platforms ( META ) that has Meta committing to spending an additional $21 billion on AI cloud infrastructure provided by the former on top of a prior arrangement that had Meta spending $14.2 billion. Incredible. This new deal will run from 2027 through 2031. The previous smaller deal runs through 2031 as well. Core Weave's data centers run on hundreds of thousands on Nvidia ( NVDA ) designed AI-capable GPUs. This provides for hyperscalers, the space and scale required to rapidly expand capacity as the scramble to meet an insatiable and still increasing demand for all things AI continues. Meta is not the only hyperscaler serviced by CoreWeave as OpenAI, Alphabet's ( GOOGL ) Google and Microsoft ( MSFT ) are also clients. There's More... Also on Thursday morning, CoreWeave announced plans to raise $3 billion through a private offering of convertible senior notes. The initial purchasers of these notes will have a 13-day period to exercise an option to buy up to an additional $450 million in notes. The notes, which are unsecured, will mature in 2031 unless repurchased, redeemed or converted to equity. The interest rate and conversion price will be determined when the offering closes and the notes are priced. Earnings CoreWeave is expected to report in about a month. At the moment, consensus is for an adjusted EPS of -$1.00 or a GAAP EPS of -$1.26 on revenue of slightly less than $2 billion. That top-line expectation would be good for annual growth of better than 100%. The GAAP EPS number would compare well to the -$1.49 posted for the year-ago period. Interestingly, this consensus sales projection stands as 14 of the 26 sell-side analysts that I know of that cover CRWV have revised their quarterly projections lower. Twelve analysts have left their numbers unrevised. Readers may recall that back in February, CoreWeave issued full year revenue guidance of $12 billion to $13 billion, but for capex spending of $30 billion to $35 billion. Does this deal (and others) improve that imbalance? The company was, at that time, also projecting an annualized run-rate of $17 billion to $19 billion in revenue by year end and over"

    "published": "2026-04-09T13:35:00Z",
    "content": "FinancialContent - CoreWeave (CRWV): The $21 Billion AI Factory Powering the Meta Partnership Recent Quotes View Full List My Watchlist Create Watchlist Indicators DJI Nasdaq Composite Standard & Poors 500 Gold Crude Oil Markets Stocks ETFs Tools Markets: Overview News Currencies International Treasuries CoreWeave (CRWV): The $21 Billion AI Factory Powering the Meta Partnership By: Finterra April 09, 2026 at 09:35 AM EDT Date: April 9, 2026 Introduction As the global \"AI Arms Race\" transitions from a frantic sprint to a sustained, multi-decade marathon, one name has emerged as the indispensable ironmonger of the modern era: CoreWeave (Nasdaq: CRWV). Just over a year since its blockbuster initial public offering, the company has transformed from a niche GPU provider into a high-stakes infrastructure powerhouse. The focal point of investor attention today is the staggering $21 billion partnership recently signed with Meta Platforms (Nasdaq: META), a deal that solidifies CoreWeave\u2019s role as the primary \"AI Factory\" for the world's most data-hungry tech giants. By providing the raw, specialized computational power necessary to fuel next-generation Large Language Models (LLMs) and real-time inference, CoreWeave has positioned itself as the \"Gold Standard\" of specialized cloud computing, challenging the dominance of the traditional hyperscale trio\u2014Amazon, Microsoft, and Google. Historical Background CoreWeave\u2019s origins are as unconventional as its current trajectory. Founded in 2017 by Michael Intrator, Brian Venturo, and Brannin McBee, the company began its life not in the AI space, but in the volatile world of cryptocurrency mining. Operating out of a small data center in New Jersey, CoreWeave was once the largest Ethereum miner in North America. However, the leadership team realized early on that their true asset was not the cryptocurrency they produced, but the technical expertise they gained in managing high-density GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) clusters at scale. In 2019, anticipating the rise of complex machine learning workloads, the company performed a strategic pivot that would define its future: it began transitioning its fleet from consumer-grade mining cards to enterprise-grade NVIDIA GPUs. This foresight allowed CoreWeave to build a \"GPU-native\" cloud architecture long before the 2023 generative AI explosion made \"GPU\" a household term. Business Model CoreWeave operates a \"specialized cloud\" model, which differs fundamentally from general-purpose cloud providers like Amazon Web Services (AWS). While AWS aims to provide everything from storage to website hosting, CoreWeave focuses exclusively on high-performance compute (HPC) workloads\u2014specifically AI training and inference, visual effects rendering, and molecular modeling. Revenue Sources: Reservation Contracts: The bulk of CoreWeave's revenue comes from multi-year contracts (often 3 to 5 years) where customers \"reserve\" large blocks of GPUs. This provides the company with exceptional revenue visibility and a massive backlog, currently estimated at over $66 billion. On-Demand Compute: A smaller portion of revenue is generated by hourly rentals of GPUs for shorter-term projects. Value-Added Services: Managed Kubernetes services and high-performance networking solutions (using InfiniBand) tailored for massive AI clusters. The company\u2019s customer base has evolved from small AI startups to Tier-1 technology companies like Meta, Mistral, and Anthropic, alongside substantial sub-leasing arrangements with"

From Electrons to Bits\u2122 \u2190 Back to Home Markets CoreWeave Signs $21B Meta AI Cloud Deal as It Seeks Another $4B Debt Financing By Wolfie Zhao \u2022 Apr 9, 2026 \u2022 2 min read CoreWeave has struck a $21 billion expansion deal with Meta to supply AI cloud capacity through 2032, alongside unveiling plans to raise more than $4 billion in fresh debt to fund its compute buildout. The agreement extends an existing relationship between the two companies and will see CoreWeave provide dedicated AI capacity across multiple sites, including early deployments of NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform systems. CoreWeave said on Thursday that the infrastructure is designed to support Meta\u2019s increasingly complex AI workloads, reflecting intensifying demand among hyperscalers for high-performance computing capacity. The deal shows how long-term, contract-backed revenue streams are becoming central to AI infrastructure providers as they scale capital-intensive data center footprints. CoreWeave said the capacity will be distributed across locations to improve resilience and performance. The announcement comes as CoreWeave simultaneously moves to secure additional financing. The company said it intends to offer $3 billion of convertible senior notes due 2032, with an option for buyers to purchase an additional $450 million. It also plans a separate $1.25 billion issuance of senior unsecured notes due 2031. The convertible notes will carry terms including cash interest payments and the option for holders to convert into cash, shares, or a combination of both, with final pricing to be determined. CoreWeave said it expects to use part of the proceeds to fund capped call transactions aimed at limiting shareholder dilution from potential conversions, with the remainder earmarked for general corporate purposes. Proceeds from the $1.25 billion senior notes may also be used to refinance existing debt, suggesting the company\u2019s active management of its capital structure as it scales. The twin debt offerings follow a broader wave of financing across the AI infrastructure sector, where developers are racing to secure capital to meet surging demand from large technology companies. CoreWeave has emerged as one of the most aggressive builders of GPU-backed cloud capacity, having secured a $8.5 billion delayed-draw term loan backed by GPU infrastructure.     "content": "Meta and CoreWeave Seal $21 Billion Deal for AI Inference Skip to content International Home International Tech & Nature Overview Channels AI & Robots Crypto Ecosystem Fintech Health International Investors Mobility People Startups Events USA Meta and CoreWeave Seal $21 Billion Deal for AI Inference Jakob Steinschaden , co-written by newsrooms.ai 09. April 2026, 13:41 Rechenzentrum von Meta Platforms. \u00a9 Meta Platforms American cloud provider CoreWeave and tech giant Meta Platforms have concluded an expanded, long-term agreement for the provision of AI computing capacity. The contract is valued at approximately 21 billion US dollars and runs through December 2032. The deal is considered one of the largest agreements in the field of AI infrastructure and underscores the growing demand for specialized computing power in the industry. What Was Agreed CoreWeave, which has been trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker CRWV since its IPO, will provide Meta with dedicated cloud capacity across multiple locations. The agreement includes, among other things, initial deployments of the new NVIDIA platform \u201cVera Rubin,\u201d one of the most powerful next-generation GPU architectures. The distributed approach across multiple data centers is designed to optimize performance, resilience, and scalability for Meta\u2019s AI operations. The agreement builds on and significantly expands an already existing business relationship between the two companies. Further details were disclosed in a mandatory filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The Shift from Training to Inference Particularly noteworthy is the strategic focus of the deal. The primary emphasis is no longer on training new AI models, but on operating them at scale \u2014 what is known as inference. This involves using already-trained models to answer queries in real time, generate content, or make decisions. This shift reflects an industry-wide development. While massive investments flowed into the training of large language models in recent years, the focus is increasingly shifting toward the productive use of these models in real-world applications. Inference workloads place their own demands on infrastructure: they require low latency, high availability, and the ability to process millions of requests simultaneously. \u201cThis is another example of leading companies choosing CoreWeave\u2019s AI cloud to run their most demanding workloads.\u201d (Michael Intrator, Co-Founder and CEO of CoreWeave) Why Inference Is Becoming the New Key Discipline The transition from training to inference has several causes. First, the major foundation models are now largely developed and are being integrated into products and services. Second, the number of users of AI-powered applications is growing rapidly, increasing the demand for scalable computing power for ongoing operations. Third, the cost of inference at a growing user base is a decisive competitive factor. Scaling in operation: Companies like Meta must keep AI models available in real time for hundreds of millions of users. Specialized hardware: Inference workloads benefit from GPU clusters optimized for throughput and efficiency. Distributed infrastructure: Multiple data center locations reduce latency and increase resilience. Long-term planning reliability: Multi-year contracts like this one allow companies to build their AI strategy on a stable infrastructure foundation. Context and"

The massive spending commitment, disclosed in an SEC filing , signals how far big tech companies will go to secure the computing power needed to train next-generation AI models - and it's reshaping the entire cloud infrastructure landscape in the process. Meta is going all-in on AI infrastructure, and the bill is staggering. The social media giant just committed an additional $21 billion to specialized GPU cloud provider CoreWeave , according to regulatory filings that reveal the true scale of what it takes to compete in the AI arms race. The commitment spans 2027 through 2032, locking in six years of infrastructure capacity at a time when GPU availability has become the most precious commodity in tech. It's a bold bet that positions CoreWeave - a relatively young player that started as a cryptocurrency mining operation - alongside cloud infrastructure giants like Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud. It is also preparing a separate $1.25 billion offering of senior unsecured notes due 2031. The convertible notes will include cash interest payments and give holders the option to convert into cash, shares, or a combination of both, with final pricing yet to be set. CoreWeave said part of the proceeds will go toward capped call transactions designed to limit dilution from potential conversions, while the remaining funds will be used for general corporate purposes. Funds raised from the unsecured notes may also be used to refinance existing obligations, indicating a continued effort to manage its capital structure while scaling operations. The financing push comes amid a wider trend across the AI infrastructure sector, where companies are securing large pools of capital to meet rising demand from hyperscalers.     "content": "CoreWeave lands essential $21 billion Meta AI deal News Entertainment Culture Business Health IQ Beauty Videos News Entertainment Culture Business Health IQ Beauty Videos Close Open Search Search [wpcode id=\"1725568\"] Home \u00bb Business CoreWeave lands essential $21 billion Meta AI deal Meta\u2019s expanded CoreWeave deal signals a fierce commitment to winning the AI infrastructure race. By David Kesiena Apr 09, 2026 8:23 am Photo credit: shutterstock/PJ McDonnell Meta\u2019s AI ambitions just got a significant financial lift. The social media giant has committed an additional $21 billion to CoreWeave, a leading AI cloud infrastructure provider, expanding a partnership that underscores just how intensely major technology companies are competing to build and deploy artificial intelligence at scale. A deal years in the making Meta and CoreWeave have worked together since 2023, but their latest agreement takes that relationship to an entirely new level. The new contract runs from 2027 through December 2032, building on an earlier arrangement worth $14.2 billion that extends through 2031. Together, the two deals represent a combined commitment of more than $35 billion, making CoreWeave one of Meta\u2019s most consequential infrastructure partners. CoreWeave operates large-scale data centers filled with Nvidia graphics processing units, the specialized chips that power modern AI systems. The company belongs to a growing class of cloud providers, often referred to as neoclouds, that rent access to high-end AI processors to some of the biggest names in tech, including Google, Microsoft and OpenAI. The new agreement will include deployments of Nvidia\u2019s Vera Rubin computing platform, spread across multiple data center locations to improve performance and resilience for Meta\u2019s operations. Why Meta keeps spending Meta\u2019s investment in CoreWeave comes as the company races to close the gap with rivals in the AI model space. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google currently lead that market, and Meta has been channeling enormous resources into its own efforts, including the launch of a Superintelligence Labs group focused on building next-generation AI. The company recently unveiled a new AI model called Muse Spark as part of that broader push. The scale of Meta\u2019s infrastructure spending is hard to overstate. The company plans to invest between $115 billion and $135 billion in capital expenditures this year alone, nearly double what it spent in 2024. Earlier this year, it also announced a $10 billion investment in a new data center in Texas. Despite building its own facilities, Meta continues to rely on CoreWeave for additional capacity. That approach reflects the sheer scale of demand the industry is navigating and gives Meta the flexibility to expand quickly without waiting for its own construction timelines to catch up. What this means for CoreWeave The expanded deal is a major win for CoreWeave, which went public on the Nasdaq in March 2025. The company\u2019s stock has climbed 24% so far this year, well ahead of the broader S&P 500, which has slipped roughly 1% over the same period. The agreement also helps CoreWeave reduce its financial reliance on Microsoft , which accounted for 62% of its total"

    "content": "CoreWeave (CRWV) signs $21 billion AI cloud deal with Meta | Grafa Skip to main content Hub News Signals Market Economy Learn Channel Company Livestream Grafa TV Quote Assets Quote Settings United States Australia Crypto Home news united states coreweave meta cloud expansion deal CoreWeave secures massive $21B AI cloud agreement with Meta Platforms Tech CoreWeave secures massive $21B AI cloud agreement with Meta Platforms Written by Mahathir Bayena Published Apr. 9 2026 Last Updated Apr. 9 2026 Discover more United States News Share CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), a specialized provider of high-performance cloud infrastructure for artificial intelligence, announced on April 9, 2026, a transformative long-term agreement with Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META). The deal, valued at approximately $21 billion, secures dedicated AI cloud capacity for Meta through December 2032 and represents a significant expansion of the existing partnership between the two companies. The agreement underscores the intensifying demand for the specialized hardware and infrastructure required to train and deploy next-generation large-scale AI models. Under the terms of the contract, CoreWeave will deploy dedicated capacity across multiple geographic locations. This distributed infrastructure strategy is designed to maximize operational resilience and provide the low-latency scalability necessary for Meta\u2019s increasingly complex AI workloads. Notably, the deployment will include some of the industry\u2019s first implementations of the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform. By integrating NVIDIA\u2019s latest high-performance computing architecture, the partnership aims to provide Meta with the foundational power needed to advance its generative AI capabilities and metaverse ambitions. For Meta, the deal provides a guaranteed, long-term supply of compute power at a time when global demand for high-end GPUs continues to outstrip availability. The partnership allows Meta to augment its internal data center capacity with CoreWeave\u2019s specialized cloud, ensuring the company can maintain its pace of innovation in a competitive AI landscape. CoreWeave had previously booked a $14.2 billion deal back in September that included an option to expand the commitment, which has been exercised with today\u2019s announcement along with new compute purchased. CoreWeave recently closed a financing deal that management billed as the first of its kind, as it was backed by its chips and Meta\u2019s AI compute purchase. This ability to effectively borrow Meta\u2019s superior creditworthiness helped CoreWeave reduce its cost of debt. Separately, CoreWeave also announced that it intends to issue $3 billion in senior convertible notes due in 2032 and $1.25 billion in senior notes due in 2031 in separate private offerings. \u201cAs spending on AI infrastructure continues to accelerate so does the need for additional debt funding, with both Meta and CoreWeave likely to continue to tap debt markets as their cloud capacity agreement expands,\u201d wrote Bloomberg Intelligence credit analysts Robert Schiffman and Alex Reid. Author Ananthu C U 09 Apr 2026, 13:00 PM CoreWeave jumps as $21 billion Meta AI cloud deal boosts outlook. Meta deal highlights rising demand for AI infrastructure services. Debt, new note offerings remain key focus for CoreWeave investors. Shares of CoreWeave rose on Thursday after the company announced an expanded long-term agreement with Meta Platforms valued at approximately $21 billion (approx. \u20a629.1 trillion), underscoring strong demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The deal extends CoreWeave\u2019s role as a cloud provider for Meta\u2019s AI initiatives through December 2032, building on an earlier agreement signed last year. The latest development highlights the growing importance of large-scale computing capacity as technology firms ramp up investments in AI deployment. In premarket trading, CoreWeave shares rose as much as 4.7% to around $93.10, while Meta stock also moved 1.8% higher. The gains came despite a softer broader market backdrop, with futures on major US indices edging lower. Expanded Meta deal signals rising AI infrastructure demand Under the agreement, CoreWeave will provide dedicated AI cloud capacity to Meta across multiple locations, supporting the development and deployment of advanced AI systems. Some of these deployments will include Nvidia\u2019s latest Vera Rubin AI platforms , reflecting the rapid evolution of hardware capabilities in the sector. The expanded partnership follows an earlier deal worth about $14.2 billion (approx. \u20a619.7 trillion) signed last fall, and Meta will also exercise an option for additional capacity included in that agreement. \u201cThis is another example that leading companies are choosing CoreWeave\u2019s AI cloud to run their most demanding workloads,\u201d said CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator. The announcement highlights a broader shift within the AI industry from model training to inference\u2014the phase where AI systems are actively used to perform tasks and generate outputs. This transition is driving sustained demand for scalable, high-performance computing infrastructure. CoreWeave said the agreement reflects accelerating demand for infrastructure capable of supporting increasingly complex and large-scale AI workloads, positioning the company as a key player in the evolving ecosystem. Lifestyle Leadership \u2709\ufe0f Emails \ud83c\udfa7 Podcasts Untitled Can IREN's 150K GPU Fleet Drive $3.7B AI Cloud ARR Target in 2026? IREN is betting on 150,000 GPUs to reach $3.7B AI cloud ARR by 2026, with $2.3B already under contract and more customer talks underway. Originally published on Zacks Investment Research Share to X Share to Facebook Share to Reddit Share to Email Share to Link Share to X Share to Facebook Share to Reddit Share to Email Share to Link Add Quartz on Google IREN Limited IREN is increasing its AI cloud capacity to 150,000 graphics processing units (GPUs), which management believes is the key to support its target of more than $3.7 billion in AI cloud annualized run-rate (ARR) revenues by the end of 2026. IREN's latest expansion includes a purchase agreement of more than 50,000 NVIDIA B300 GPUs. This expands the company\u2019s total GPU fleet to 150,000 GPUs. These GPUs are expected to be deployed in Mackenzie, British Columbia and Childress, Texas, using IREN\u2019s existing air-cooled data center capacity. The company plans to deploy the GPUs in phases during the second half of 2026. The target looks possible because IREN already has a good amount of AI cloud revenues under contract. During its fiscal second-quarter 2026 earnings call, management said the company had about $2.3 billion of annualized revenue run rate under contract. This includes the Microsoft $MSFT deal and about $0.4 billion of contracted revenues at Prince George. Management also said customer demand remains strong and that the company is in multiple advanced talks for large-scale deployments. Related Content Amazon CEO Andy Jassy defends AI spending: 'We're not going to be conservative in how we play this' BYD and KFC will pair fast EV charging with drive-thru dining in China IREN also looks better placed from a funding point of view. The company said it has secured $9.3 billion of funding over the past eight months through customer prepayments, convertible notes, GPU leasing and GPU financing. This matters because AI cloud expansion needs heavy spending upfront. For the latest GPU orders, IREN expects about $3.5 billion of additional capex, including GPUs, servers, storage, networking, labor and other related equipment. For now, the target depends on execution. IREN's ability to deploy these GPUs on time, sign more customer contracts and ramp customer workloads through the second half of 2026 will be the key to hitting the target of $3.7 billion in AI cloud revenues by 2026. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2026 and 2027 indicates revenue growth of around 95% and 193.9%, respectively. IREN Stock Faces Stiff Competition IREN faces intense competition from Applied Digital APLD and TeraWulf WULF in the AI infrastructure space. In January 2026, Applied Digital announced that it had started construction on Delta Forge 1, a large AI data center campus in a southern U.S. state."

IRENs , Ambitions IREN's AI Ambitions Face Critical Test Amid Market Skepticism 09.04.2026 - 15:24:33 | boerse-global.de IREN races to launch Texas power substation, a key test for its $9.3B AI cloud pivot, as Bitcoin mining revenue falls and share dilution concerns weigh on the stock. IREN's AI Ambitions Face Critical Test Amid Market Skepticism - Foto: \u00fcber boerse-global.de A surprise geopolitical truce provided a fleeting boost, but for IREN Ltd., the real battle for investor confidence is being fought on the ground in Texas. The company\u2019s aggressive pivot from Bitcoin mining to artificial intelligence infrastructure is entering its most critical phase, marked by a massive capital outlay and a looming proof-of-concept deadline that has left the stock languishing well below its highs. The immediate catalyst for a recent share price bounce to $39.50 was macro-driven. Announcements of a two-week ceasefire in the Middle East by US President Donald Trump sparked a broad market rally, with the Dow Jones posting its strongest trading day in a year. Bitcoin surged to $72,700, forcing short sellers to cover nearly $600 million in positions. This dynamic environment offered IREN shares a welcome, if temporary, reprieve from a steep sell-off that has left the stock trading roughly 54% below its all-time high. Beneath this short-term volatility lies a stark operational reality. The company is racing to prove its new business model, and all eyes are on the imminent launch of its 1.4-gigawatt Sweetwater 1 substation in West Texas. This milestone, originally slated for October 2026, is now scheduled for April\u2014a full six months ahead of plan. Institutional investors view the successful commissioning of this power infrastructure as the essential feasibility test for IREN\u2019s AI cloud ambitions, especially after the absence of a new major customer deal last quarter eroded confidence. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying IREN? Financing this transformation requires staggering sums. Over the past eight months, IREN has secured funding commitments totaling $9.3 billion. A cornerstone of this effort is a $1.9 billion prepayment from Microsoft, part of a five-year, $9.7 billion contract for 200 megawatts of data center capacity. The company also secured $3.6 billion in GPU financing at a 6% interest rate in its second fiscal quarter. To support its hardware expansion, IREN ordered an additional 50,000 Nvidia B300 graphics cards in March"

IRENs , Billion IREN's $6 Billion Funding Gamble Tests Investor Faith in AI Ambitions 09.04.2026 - 04:32:44 | boerse-global.de IREN's aggressive $6B capital raise for AI data centers risks diluting shareholders by nearly half, as the stock falls 23% despite securing $2.3B in contracted revenue. IREN's $6 Billion Funding Gamble Tests Investor Faith in AI Ambitions - Foto: \u00fcber boerse-global.de The data center operator IREN is navigating a precarious path, caught between the demands of financing a massive infrastructure build-out and the immediate concerns of its shareholders. At the heart of this tension is a capital-raising program that could dilute existing investors by nearly half, even as the company races to secure its position in the competitive AI cloud services arena. Investor apprehension is palpable in the stock's performance. Shares have retreated approximately 23% over the past three months, trading recently at $35.74\u2014a far cry from its 52-week high of $76.87. This pressure stems partly from weakness in the Bitcoin mining sector and, more significantly, from an ongoing at-the-market (ATM) equity offering. The program authorizes the issuance of new shares worth up to $6 billion, a substantial figure against a current market capitalization of roughly $11.86 billion. The proceeds are earmarked for large-scale GPU deployments and the construction of additional data centers. Despite the downtrend, derivatives traders have shown fleeting optimism. On April 7, total options volume reached 120,220 contracts, with 71.79% of the activity in bullish call options. A notable cluster of over 9,000 contracts was concentrated in $35 strike calls expiring on April 10, suggesting a short-term bet on stabilization around that level. The capital is fueling an aggressive transformation. IREN's operational pivot hinges on the imminent activation of its Sweetwater-1 substation, a 1,400-megawatt facility slated to come online this month. This infrastructure is foundational for the company's shift toward hyperscale AI cloud services. By the end of 2026, IREN aims to deploy 150,000 GPUs, a capacity it believes can generate significant annual recurring revenue (ARR). Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying IREN? However, the specifics of that revenue target are under scrutiny. The company communicates two distinct figures. Its officially confirmed goal is $3.4 billion in ARR by late 2026, based on executed contracts and advanced customer negotiations for its Mackenzie and Canal Flats sites. This target implies"

CTech 09:26, 09.04.26 AI21 Labs is in acquisition talks once again, this time with AI infrastructure company Nebius, according to a report by The Information, months after earlier negotiations with Nvidia failed to result in a deal. Calcalist previously reported that the Israeli startup had held advanced discussions with Nvidia at a reported valuation of $2 billion to $3 billion, above its last known valuation of $1.4 billion from 2023. Those talks reached senior levels but ultimately did not materialize into a transaction. 1 View gallery AI21 Labs founders. ( Photo: Orel Cohen ) In January, co-founder and chairman Amnon Shashua confirmed that AI21 was engaged in discussions with Nvidia as well as other potential buyers, indicating that the company was formally exploring strategic options. Founded in 2017 by Shashua, Professor Yoav Shoham and Ori Goshen, AI21 was among the early companies developing large-scale language models. However, it has struggled in recent years to keep pace with leading AI developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic. The company has since narrowed its focus to enterprise applications, emphasizing accuracy and reliability. It discontinued development of its consumer product, Wordtune, and now centers on offerings such as its Maestro platform and a recently introduced reasoning model. Annual revenue is estimated at around $50 million. Related articles: \u201cThere are talks with Nvidia and others\u201d: Shashua confirms AI21 acquisition discussions AI21 never closed its reported $300 million round as Nvidia weighs an acquisition Nvidia in advanced talks to acquire AI21 in $2-3 billion deal focused on talent AI21 employs roughly 200 people, down from about 260 in 2023, after scaling back expansion plans. Much of the interest in the company has been attributed to its workforce, which includes highly trained AI researchers. Published on: Apr 5, 2026 Author: Sunlight Xiang Share article: Two tech giants are backing the same dark horse in AI cloud infrastructure. Meta signed a $27 billion deal. Nvidia invested $2 billion. And Nebius Group (NBIS) \u2013 up nearly 400% over the past year \u2013 is leaving rival CoreWeave (up 109%) in the dust. With a $25.2 billion market cap, Nebius is still smaller than CoreWeave\u2019s $40.7 billion. But the gap is closing fast. Dual Heavyweight Backing In mid-March, Nebius landed a five-year AI infrastructure agreement with Meta worth up to $27 billion \u2013 $12 billion for dedicated capacity plus a $15 billion option for additional purchases. Around the same time, Nvidia announced a $2 billion strategic stake, helping Nebius deploy over 5 gigawatts of Nvidia systems through 2030. Notably, Nvidia already owned more than 12% of CoreWeave as of late 2025. Betting on both horses says everything about how hot this race is. Scale vs. Speed CoreWeave is still the larger player: $40.7 billion market cap, 43 data centers, 850 megawatts of live power. Nebius had just 170 MW at the end of 2025 but plans to hit 800 MW to 1 GW by end of 2026. But growth tells a different story. Nebius stock: +400% in 12 months CoreWeave stock: +109% in the same period Revenue in Q4: Nebius surged 547% year-over-year to $228 million. CoreWeave grew 110% to $1.57 billion. Both Burning Cash to Grow Neither is profitable yet. Both are spending heavily on GPUs and data centers. Nebius (Q4) CoreWeave (Q4) Net loss $173M $284M Quarterly capex $2B+ $8.2B CoreWeave expects 2026 revenue of $12-13 billion, backed by over $46 billion in contracts with OpenAI and Meta. Nebius holds major deals with Meta ($27B) and Microsoft (up to $19.4B). Risks and the Bigger Picture AI compute rental prices are up 40% since October \u2013 demand remains strong. Nebius recently raised $4 billion in convertible notes and is building a 300 MW data center in Finland, targeting 3 GW of contracted business by 2026. But high capex and fierce competition mean volatility is guaranteed. Nebius offers faster growth, elite customers, and Nvidia\u2019s blessing. CoreWeave still leads in scale and execution. For investors, Nebius is a high-upside bet: if it converts its backlog into profits, the sky\u2019s the limit. If not,"

Nebius , Stock Nebius Stock: A High-Wire Act of Explosive Growth and Mounting Skepticism 09.04.2026 - 15:24:33 | boerse-global.de Nebius shares surged 485% in a year, fueled by AI deals with Microsoft & Meta and a $2B Nvidia investment, despite massive losses and high execution risks. Nebius Stock: A High-Wire Act of Explosive Growth and Mounting Skepticism - Foto: \u00fcber boerse-global.de Nebius shares surged on Tuesday, climbing as high as $128 on above-average volume. The rally was fueled by a potent mix: a bullish endorsement from CNBC's Jim Cramer, who labeled the company part of his \"data center of the future\" category, and concrete steps in its global expansion strategy. The stock closed the regular session up 4.32% at $117.40, capping a remarkable 485% gain over the past twelve months. The company\u2019s growth metrics are staggering. Revenue soared 479% year-over-year in 2025, with a particularly sharp 547% jump to $227.7 million in the fourth quarter alone. This trajectory is underpinned by a massive backlog exceeding $20 billion, anchored by multi-year contracts with tech titans Microsoft ($19.4 billion) and Meta ($12 billion). A strategic $2 billion investment from Nvidia further validates its position in the AI infrastructure race. Management aims for an annualized revenue run rate of $7 to $9 billion by the end of 2026, with more than half already under contract. To fulfill these commitments, Nebius is accelerating its geographic footprint. The appointment of former Cloudflare and Twilio executive John Haarer as General Manager for Asia-Pacific and Japan marks a pivot from market exploration to active expansion from a Singapore base, targeting key markets like Japan, South Korea, and India. This builds on its existing networks in Europe and North America. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Nebius? This breakneck growth, however, comes at an immense cost and carries significant operational risk. The company\u2019s GAAP net loss widened to $249.6 million last quarter. Capital expenditures are exploding, hitting $2.06 billion in Q4 and projected to reach $16 to $20 billion for 2026\u2014dwarfing its forecasted annual revenue of $3 to $3.4 billion. Roughly 40% of the required funding must still be secured through additional debt, asset-backed financing, or equity raises. Search Blog Computer, Electronic And Optical Products Electronic Components And Boards Multichip Integrated Circuits: Memories Apr 6, 2026 AI Infrastructure Stocks: Broadcom, Nvidia, Nebius Lead 2030 Data Center Buildout According to a report from Yahoo Finance, artificial intelligence represents a significant long-term investment opportunity with broad economic implications. The analysis suggests that public investors might consider companies supplying computing components, as these firms stand to benefit from the AI expansion irrespective of which specific AI developers ultimately succeed. The report highlights three stocks as prominent choices in the current AI infrastructure buildout: Broadcom , Nvidia , and Nebius . These companies are noted for having substantial and expanding revenue streams. Broadcom and Nvidia are identified as competitors within the same market segment, though the scale of the opportunity is considered sufficient for multiple participants. Industry projections indicate data center spending will reach very high levels by 2030. Both Broadcom and Nvidia are positioned to secure a significant share of the computing power demand within this trend. Nvidia's graphics processing units are described as the established standard for AI computing, a leadership position viewed as highly secure. Broadcom, in contrast, pursues a different strategy by collaborating with clients to design custom AI chips tailored for specific workloads. This approach can yield performance and cost advantages for certain applications, and such custom chips are seen as potentially complementary to Nvidia's general-purpose GPUs. The analysis concludes that both companies are poised for considerable growth in the coming period, a prospect that may not be fully reflected in their current market valuations.     "content": "Nebius in talks to acquire AI21 Labs - report - Globes \" /> \" /> \" /> \" /> search G Front News Comment Features MARKET ECONOMY ENERGY HEALTHCARE TECH REAL ESTATE START UPS AEROSPACE & DEFENSE CHEMICALS & PLASTICS FINANCIAL SERVICES MERGERS & ACQUISITIONS POLITICS TELECOMS, MEDIA & MARKETING TOURISM TRANSPORT & INFRASTRUCTURE Front > News Nebius in talks to acquire AI21 Labs - report AI21 Labs founders Amnon Shashua, Yoav Shaham and Ori Goshen credit: Omer Hacohen Israel reopens amid uncertainty in north NewMed Energy signs MOU to sell Aphrodite gas to Egypt 9 Apr, 2026 10:12 Assaf Gilead \u201cThe Information\u201d reports that Dutch AI cloud company Nebius is negotiating to buy the Israeli company after Nvidia pulled out of talks to buy AI21 Labs. Despite denials by the company, Israeli artificial intelligence company AI21 Labs looks set to be acquired sooner or later. The company, co-founded by Prof. Amnon Shashua, is in talks to be acquired by Dutch AI cloud provider Nebius (Nasdaq: NBIS), founded by Israelis and former Yandex executives Arkady Volozh and Roman Chernin, \"The Information\" reports. Nebius was founded in the Netherlands but has a major development center in the Alon Towers in Tel Aviv and many of the senior executives including founders Volozh and Chernin as well as COO Ophir Nave and Elena Bunina live in Israel. AI entrepreneur Dr. Kira Radinsky sits on the company\u2019s board of directors. Nebius was founded after executives at Yandex, the Russian search engine, sold most of the company's operations to a group of executives close to the Kremlin. These executives, most of whom are new immigrants who arrived in Israel after the Russian invasion of Crimea in 2014, used their cloud knowledge acquired at Yandex to establish a new operation. Today, Nebius is an AI cloud services provider, which leases data centers. One of its best-known activities in Israel is the operation of the national supercomputer in Modi'in, which is hosted on MegaDC's data center in Modi'in. Nebius currently has a market cap of $32 billion, after signing a series of huge agreements to supply GPU-based data centers to Meta and Microsoft. The company has raised hundreds of millions of dollars from Nvidia, with whom it maintains close ties. Nebius competes with CoreWeave and Crusoe, which also recently began operations in Israel. After signing a $27 billion agreement to provide AI services to Meta, Nvidia said it would invest $2 billion in Nebious.. AI21 Labs, despite previously denying talks on a sale to Nvidia, is looking for an exit after failing to penetrate the market with its language models. It has recently been gaining relative success with its AI agent management product, Maestro. AI21 Labs was given a $1.4 billion price tag in 2023, and investors in the company, including Pitango, Intel Capital, B2 Ventures, Coatue, Google and Nvidia, are estimated to be looking for a premium on the investment and hoping to sell AI21 Labs for several billion dollars. The firm has secured a strategic partnership with Nvidia , which has invested billions of dollars and provides early access to its newest computing equipment. This relationship has helped attract major corporate clients, including Meta Platforms and Microsoft , alongside individual developers. Infrastructure and Financial Growth The company has rapidly increased its data center footprint, growing from two sites in 2024 to seven by the close of 2025. Plans indicate an expansion to 16 sites by the end of 2026. This scaling is reflected in its financial performance, with the core AI business reporting a substantial year-over-year revenue increase in the final quarter of 2025. The company anticipates its annual revenue run rate will rise significantly from its level at the end of 2025. This expansion is driven by demand from large technology companies seeking rentable computing capacity. The shift reflects a growing trend among cloud and AI providers to integrate both compute capabilities and enterprise-ready software solutions. Nebius already operates an in-house large language model (LLM) research and development team, alongside its inference platform, Nebius AI Studio, which enables users to run and manage AI models efficiently. However, acquiring AI21 Labs would significantly enhance its capabilities by adding an enterprise software layer , allowing Nebius to offer more comprehensive AI solutions to businesses. By integrating AI21 Labs\u2019 expertise, Nebius could strengthen its position in the enterprise AI market , offering end-to-end solutions that combine compute power, model development, and application-level functionality. Customer demand is also a key driver behind this potential deal. Nebius has secured major contracts, including a significant agreement with Meta reportedly worth up to US$27 billion. Additionally, the company has received substantial customer prepayments, largely from Microsoft and Meta, highlighting strong demand for its AI infrastructure services. The potential acquisition underscores a broader industry shift where AI companies are evolving from infrastructure providers to full-stack AI platforms . By Sarah Motter and Chandler Watkins Published : Mar. 25, 2026 at 4:57 PM CDT Comment 0 Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google INDEPENDENCE, Mo. (KCTV) - A Jackson County judge has blocked residents from voting on a massive AI data center tax deal. Court records show that on Wednesday, March 25, Judge Jennifer M. Phillips denied the declaratory judgment and injunctive relief petition filed by three Independence residents. The residents sought to force a citywide vote on the tax incentive package tied to the Nebius data center project. ALSO READ: Residents continuing to fight after judge blocks referendum deadlines What the judge decided The court says it found that the ordinance authorizing the city to issue up to $150.6 billion in revenue bonds for the project went into effect immediately under the city charter. The provision covers ordinances related to specific contracts and bond issuances, placing them outside the reach of a public referendum. In plain terms: because the ordinance took effect the moment the council passed it on March 2 , residents had no legal window to trigger a referendum under the charter. Residents oppose the Nebius data center on March 19, 2025. Share pdf Share on linkedin Share on facebook Share on twitter Share on email Nebius Group N.V. (Nebius Group or the company; Nasdaq: NBIS), a leading AI infrastructure company, has announced the pricing of its offering of US$4.0 billion aggregate original principal amount of convertible senior notes, in two series: US$2.25 billion aggregate original principal amount of 1.250% convertible notes due 2031 (the 2031 notes) and US$1.75 billion aggregate original principal amount of 2.625% convertible notes due 2033 (the 2033 notes, and together with the 2031 notes, the notes), in a private offering to qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act of 1933. The offering was upsized from the previously announced offering size of US$3.75 billion aggregate original principal amount of the notes. The issuance and sale of the notes are expected to settle on March 20, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Nebius Group has also granted the initial purchaser an overallotment option to purchase, for settlement within a period of 13 days from, and including, the date the notes are first issued, up to an additional US$337.5 million aggregate original principal amount of 2031 notes and up to an additional US$262.5 million aggregate original principal amount of 2033 notes. The company estimates that the net proceeds from the offering of the notes will be approximately US$3.96 billion (or approximately US$4.55 billion if the initial purchaser fully exercises its option to purchase additional notes), after deducting the initial purchaser\u2019s discounts and commissions and estimated offering expenses. Latham & Watkins LLP represented the initial purchaser in the offering with a cross-border Capital Markets team led by partner Jenna Gascoyne and counsel Polina Tulupova, with associates Lexi Zintel, Rebecca Reeve, Daniel Weiss, and Joe Fitzpatrick. Advice was also provided on tax matters by partner Elena Romanova, with associate Farrah Yan. Endnotes Show All Endnotes Collapse Endnotes Contacts Jennifer M.     "content": "Nscale moves into power with AIPCorp deal, building 8GW U.S. AI campus to bypass energy bottlenecks | Edge Infrastructure Review AI Infrastructure Cloud Platforms Connectivity Data Centers Edge Computing rss linkedin facebook search search --> About News Companies Markets Directory Guides Resources Events Subscribe Search for: Search X Share X/Tweet Link Comment Nscale moves into power with AIPCorp deal, building 8GW U.S. AI campus to bypass energy bottlenecks Apr 6, 2026 | Stephen Mayhew Categories Digital Infrastructure News | Technology & Architecture UK-based neocloud Nscale recently secured the largest Series C round in European history, raising $2 billion . Nscale then made good on its full-stack AI hyperscaler vision by acquiring two key assets: American Intelligence & Power Corporation ( AIPCorp ) and the Monarch Compute Campus in West Virginia. Monarch Compute Campus will be the first state-certified AI microgrid in the U.S. It is scalable up to 8 gigawatts of clean, renewable power by 2031. \u201dNscale is a global company, and the US is the world\u2019s largest AI infrastructure market. AI infrastructure needs to be built where demand is, and right now a significant share of that demand is in the United States,\u201d says Josh Payne, CEO of Nscale. \u201cMonarch allows us to meet that demand. The acquisition builds on our existing US footprint and reflects the pace at which we are scaling to serve customers around the world.\u201d It will initially have 2 gigawatts of power capacity to be operational by 2028 to support AI infrastructure growth in the U.S. To manage the integration of energy and compute, Nscale created a new division based in Houston, Texas \u2013 Nscale Energy & Power. Nscale will be joined by the leadership and staff of AIPCorp, which has nearly a decade of experience building AI infrastructure, as it develops a global presence. The reason behind the acquisition is an attempt to resolve bottlenecks in AI compute demand with a vertically integrated power-and-compute model. Nscale specializes in scalable AI infrastructure across Europe and North America for all aspects of the AI life-cycle such as training, fine-tuning, and inference. Critics of the U.K.'s AI infrastructure buildout previously told CNBC the high cost of energy and delays in accessing the national grid were key stumbling blocks. Lawmakers in the U.K are also looking to develop new regulations around how AI models use copyrighted work. Nscale declined to comment when approached by CNBC about the project being paused. Nvidia has been approached for comment. OpenAI and Nscale are still in discussions about the project in the future, a source with direct knowledge of the matter told CNBC. David Chernicoff , Matt Vincent April 3, 2026 15 min read Key Highlights Nscale has secured over $2 billion in funding and is valued at approximately $14.6 billion, reflecting strong investor confidence in its integrated AI infrastructure approach. The company's acquisition of AIPCorp enables it to develop large-scale energy microgrids, such as the Monarch Compute Campus, designed to deliver up to 8 gigawatts of power, bypassing utility constraints. Nscale is establishing a multi-regional campus network, including sites in the US, UK, Norway, Portugal, and Finland, each tailored to regional energy, regulatory, and political advantages. Partnerships with industry leaders like Microsoft and Nvidia are central to Nscale\u2019s strategy, ensuring demand-driven development aligned with next-generation AI hardware and software platforms. The company's focus on energy certainty, through on-site generation and microgrids, aims to reduce deployment delays and create a reliable supply chain for hyperscale AI workloads. Fidelisinfra.com Rendering of the Monarch Compute Campus Nscale has moved quickly from startup to serious contender in the race to build infrastructure for the AI era. Founded in 2024, the company has positioned itself as a vertically integrated \u201cneocloud\u201d operator , combining data center development, GPU fleet ownership, and a software stack designed to deliver large-scale AI compute. That model has helped it attract backing from investors including Nvidia, and in early March 2026 the company raised another $2 billion at a reported $14.6 billion valuation. Reuters has described Nscale\u2019s approach as owning and operating its own data centers, GPUs, and software stack to support major customers including Microsoft and OpenAI. What makes Nscale especially relevant now is that it is no longer content to operate as a cloud intermediary or capacity provider. Over the past year, the company has increasingly framed itself as an AI hyperscaler and AI factory builder, seeking to combine land, power, data center shells, GPU procurement, customer offtake, and software services into a single integrated platform. Its acquisition of American Intelligence & Power Corporation, or AIPCorp , is the clearest signal yet of that shift, bringing energy infrastructure directly into the center of Nscale\u2019s business model.     "content": "Microsoft is embracing off-grid gas for West Virginia data centers | Latitude Media Microsoft is embracing off-grid gas for West Virginia data centers | Latitude Media Subscribe Covering the new frontiers of the energy transition Tech Grid edge Solar Energy storage Artificial intelligence Data centers Carbon removal Hydrogen Emerging tech Geothermal Nuclear See all Resilience Markets U.S. market Global markets Policy Regulation Research See all Deals Venture capital Project finance Corporates Mergers and acquisitions Government funding See all Tech Grid edge Solar Energy storage Artificial intelligence Data centers Carbon removal Hydrogen Emerging tech Geothermal Nuclear See all Resilience Markets U.S. market Global markets Policy Regulation Research See all Deals Venture capital Project finance Corporates Mergers and acquisitions Government funding See all Podcasts Events Research Resources Latitude Studios About Newsletter Authors Staff Careers Advertise Contact Tech Markets Deals Podcasts Events Research Resources Analysis Corporates DATA CENTERS Microsoft is embracing off-grid gas for West Virginia data centers The hyperscaler's deal with \"neocloud\" developer Nscale takes advantage of a new state law to bypass grid delays. Catherine Boudreau April 1, 2026 Add Latitude on Google Photo credit: Aerovista Luchtfotografie / Shutterstock West Virginia, with its ready supply of cheap gas and a new law allowing off-grid data centers, may be the next frontier for big-name customers like Microsoft. The hyperscaler in March signed a \u201cletter of intent\u201d to secure nearly 1.4 gigawatts of power from a microgrid project underway in Mason County, W. Va. The developer, Nscale \u2014 a two-year-old startup building AI compute campuses in the U.S. and Europe \u2014 said it plans to deploy hundreds of gas generators by the first half of 2028. The deal marks the first time that Microsoft has committed to a fully off-grid, gas-powered data center at the gigawatt scale, said Olivia Wang, a research analyst at Sightline who\u2019s tracking the global data center pipeline . Previously, she added, the company has mainly used gas generators for backup capacity in new data center builds, not as a primary energy source. Nscale took over the project when it acquired American Intelligence & Power Corporation, which specialized in behind-the-meter microgrids for AI data centers. Stuart Pann, senior advisor at Nscale, told Latitude Media in an interview at CERAWeek that the company saw a lot of opportunity in West Virginia because it sits atop the Marcellus Formation, the largest gas field in the country that spans Appalachia. \u201cWe\u2019re taking advantage of the geographic location of this facility, which can have four separate pipelines fed into it. There\u2019s a chance to make this a gas hub, in the same way Henry Hub is,\u201d Pann said, referring to a gas pipeline interchange in Louisiana that serves as a price benchmark for North America. A Microsoft spokesperson said the company takes a portfolio approach to energy for its global AI infrastructure based on local conditions, grid readiness, and long\u2011term goals. That flexibility allows Microsoft to \u201cbring capacity online faster, ensure reliability, and limit strain on local grids while continuing to invest in"

Your phone knows what to do when it crosses a border. Without instruction or intervention, it finds a local cell tower, authenticates, and continues, seamlessly extending the session as you move around outside your home. It is an unremarkable moment, repeated billions of times a day, made possible by decades of inter-carrier agreements, shared standards, and a collective decision by an entire industry to build for interoperability rather than isolation. \u200d Many enterprise AI workloads today are anchored to fixed compute in a specific geography: powerful within their boundaries, but brittle at the edges. When demand spikes in a different region, when a data center fails, or when a regulatory constraint requires local processing, the system either degrades or breaks. The architectural model that underpins most AI deployments was not designed for the operational demands now being placed on it. \u200d AI roaming changes that. It represents the next structural shift in AI infrastructure: the move from sovereign national AI grids to a federated, global AI fabric. \u200d And the technology to make it work already exists. \u200d What AI roaming actually means AI roaming is the ability for an inference workload to move seamlessly across providers and geographies, preserving context and continuity, without the end user or application being aware that a handoff has occurred. It is not simply multi-cloud load balancing. It is stateful, federated inference: the AI equivalent of a cellular handoff between towers. \u200d The architectural distinction matters. Kubernetes changed how the industry deploys software. Built for the web services era, it offered a clean, declarative model for managing stateless, interchangeable workloads at scale. For a decade, that model worked well. \u200d AI breaks it. \u200d Training runs are long-lived, stateful, and bound to specific GPU topologies. Inference traffic is volatile and latency-sensitive. High-performance networking is no longer optional. GPUs, network fabrics, storage, power, and cooling all have to be orchestrated as a single system. When topology is wrong, performance collapses. \u200d What we are seeing is not simply a tooling gap, but a structural mismatch: AI workloads demand HPC-class infrastructure with cloud-grade flexibility. Initiatives like the Serving Working Group , the AI Gateway WG , and ongoing work in SIG Scheduling have improved Kubernetes\u2019 viability for AI workloads over the past few years. But even with that progress, the remaining challenge is aligning increasingly capable AI software components with the physical realities of GPU topology, high-speed interconnects, and performance-sensitive infrastructure. \u200d Developers expect orchestration platforms like Kubernetes; MLOps tools such as Kubeflow and MLflow; ML frameworks including PyTorch and vLLM; interactive environments like Jupyter Notebooks; compatible APIs; and a broad ecosystem of supporting tools. They expect self-serve environments, fast iteration, and a clean path from experiment to production. They expect cost visibility, reproducibility, and zero rework. \u200d Our job is to deliver bare-metal performance without the operational drag. That means contiguous GPU pools with topology-aware scheduling, high-bandwidth interconnects built in,"

The next step is turning that foundation into sustainable AI revenue. Telco networks carry the traffic that powers the AI economy. More than half of all AI inference calls traverse mobile infrastructure. That means every query, every model response, every real-time AI interaction that hundreds of millions of users generate each day. The infrastructure telcos built is, in effect, the physical backbone of the inference economy. \u200d The edge AI market is projected to reach $118 billion by 2033, and telcos are capturing almost none of its value. \u200d That is not a temporary imbalance awaiting correction. It crystallised at a specific moment: as generative AI crossed from technical novelty into mainstream utility, cloud infrastructure economics began compounding sharply while telecom revenue remained essentially flat. The two curves have diverged. The industry that owns and operates the physical layer has yet to position itself to participate in the economic one. \u200d \u200d What changes this equation is not strategy or product positioning. It is physics. The latency requirements of real-time AI, including autonomous systems, industrial inference, agentic AI at the edge, make centralised cloud architectures structurally inadequate for the workloads that matter most. And the infrastructure that resolves those constraints is infrastructure telcos already possess . The edge imperative As AI workloads scale and move into production, many will require capabilities that extend beyond traditional cloud-only infrastructure.     "content": "News AWS Uber scales on AWS to help power millions of daily trips and train its AI models The ride-sharing giant expands its real-time infrastructure on AWS to speed up service for millions of daily riders and deliveries. Share Written by Amazon Staff 2 min read Key takeaways Graviton4 and Trainium3 are Amazon\u2019s custom-designed chips for computing and AI training. Uber uses AWS Graviton4 to help match customers with drivers in milliseconds. Uber pilots AWS Trainium3 to build faster, smarter AI predictions and models. Uber scales Trip Serving Zones on AWS to help handle demand spikes for rides and deliveries. Uber, the world's largest ride-sharing and on-demand delivery company, is expanding its infrastructure and artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities on Amazon Web Services (AWS) . Uber is using AWS Graviton instances to support more of its Trip Serving Zones, the real-time infrastructure behind every ride and delivery, and has started pilot training some AI models on Trainium \u2014enabling faster rider and delivery matching, global demand handling, and smarter, more personalized experiences for millions of daily users. Every time you open Uber and request a ride or delivery, a series of split-second decisions happens behind the scenes. Which driver is closest? What's the fastest route? How long will it actually take? Getting those answers right instantly\u2014for millions of people at once\u2014requires the right infrastructure for Uber to deliver these capabilities at scale during rush hour and major events. How Graviton helps power millions of trips in real time Uber\u2019s Trip Serving Zones are part of the system that makes sure every ride and delivery runs smoothly, which requires making millions of predictions and processing location data in milliseconds. Now, Uber is expanding its use of AWS compute, storage, and networking to help power real-time operations for Trip Serving Zones. By running more of these workloads on AWS Graviton4, Uber can reduce energy consumption while scaling rapidly during demand spikes, both reducing latency and optimizing costs. Graviton's high performance enables some of the real-time calculations that help match riders with drivers faster\u2014without compromising reliability, availability, or security. AWS Graviton4 \"Uber operates at a scale where milliseconds matter,\" said Kamran Zargahi, vice president of engineering at Uber. \"Moving more Trip Serving workloads to AWS gives us the flexibility to match riders and drivers faster and handle delivery demand spikes without disruption.\u201d Improving Uber rides at scale with AWS Trainium chips Uber has also begun experimenting with AWS Trainium3 to train some of the AI models that help power its apps. These models analyze data from billions of rides and deliveries to determine which driver or courier to send, calculate arrival times, and recommend the best delivery options to the customer. Training AI at this scale requires enormous computing power\u2014Trainium provides an efficient, cost-effective way to do it. As the models learn from more trips, Uber delivers faster matches, more accurate arrival time estimates, and more personalized recommendations to customers worldwide so they can get where they are going faster and receive their deliveries sooner."

Threat Research Center Threat Research Malware Malware Cracks in the Bedrock: Escaping the AWS AgentCore Sandbox 13 min read Related Products Cortex Cortex Cloud Unit 42 AI Security Assessment Unit 42 Cloud Security Assessment Unit 42 Incident Response By: Ori Hadad Published: April 7, 2026 Categories: Malware Threat Research Tags: Agentcore Agentcore runtime AWS DNS tunneling GenAI Sandbox Share Executive Summary When researching the boundaries of cloud services, two of the main aspects that come to mind are network and identity. In this two-part series, we present our research into the boundaries and resilience of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. In this first part, we explore how AgentCore\u2019s Code Interpreter sandbox network isolation mode could be bypassed in a way that allows sending and receiving of data from external endpoints via DNS tunneling. In the second part, we explore the identity side, and how an attacker can leverage weaknesses in default identities and permissions to compromise other AgentCore agents within an AWS account and exfiltrate sensitive data from other services. To support the growing adoption of AI agents, AWS announced global availability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in late 2025. AgentCore is a framework that allows organizations to build, deploy and manage AI agents. It protects one of its most useful resources, Code Interpreters, that allows AI agents to dynamically execute code by isolating it from external network access using sandbox mode. Our discovery showed that this isolation is incomplete. We outline the steps we took to identify the sandbox bypass. We also identified a critical security regression where the AgentCore Runtime utilized a microVM Metadata Service (MMDS) that lacks session token enforcement. Prior to our disclosure and AWS's fixes, this configuration could have allowed an attacker to exploit standard web vulnerabilities, such as server-side request forgery ( SSRF ), to directly extract sensitive credentials, putting the entire environment at risk. We responsibly disclosed all findings to the AWS Security team. Following their review, AWS introduced the necessary internal remediations and outlined several important mitigation strategies for customers. Users cannot patch the managed environment directly, but can leverage the platform-level controls AWS provides. As reliance on these services grows, understanding their internal mechanics is crucial for maintaining security. Palo Alto Networks customers are better protected from the threats discussed in this article through the following products and services: Cortex AI-SPM Cortex Cloud Identity Security The Unit 42 AI Security Assessment The Unit 42 Cloud Security Assessment If you think you might have been compromised or have an urgent matter, contact the Unit 42 Incident Response team . Related Unit 42 Topics Cloud , DNS Tunneling , Sandbox , Investigation Overview: Scope, Methodology and Key Findings Our investigation focused on the Code Interpreter service provided by AgentCore , which offers an isolated sandbox compute environment for AI agents to execute their code. The sandbox mode promises an easy way to implement restrictions on network access, which"

S3 is Amazon's incredibly popular object storage service. AWS is adding file services to S3 using its Elastic File System (EFS). This provides NFS support for S3 and is a managed file storage service with no need for provisioning capacity or performance management. File storage suppliers such as NetApp and Qumulo already provide combined file and object storage services in AWS. They now face more competition. BANDF AD AWS says any NFS-based application, agent, or tool can now access and work with S3 data as a file system with no change. Specifically, S3 Files supports the NFS v4.2 and 4.1 protocols. It provides file-system-access semantics, such as read-after-write data consistency, file locking, and POSIX permissions. AWS says S3 Files provides the performance and capabilities of a file system with the scalability, durability, and cost-effectiveness of S3. Up until now, AWS customers wanting application and user file-based access to data kept in an AWS (S3) data lake needed to copy the object data into a file-based pool, either an AWS one or a third-party supplier's resource. Now they can stay entirely inside the S3 environment. Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS) provides file system semantics, file-level security, and scale built on Blob storage. ADLS supports NFS v3.0, SMB, and the Apache Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) as a data access layer. Admins can't natively combine file and object storage on the same Azure share, but the two live in the same storage account as Blob/Object storage. Google Cloud does not offer combined file and object storage services like AWS, nor does Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). BANDF AD With S3 Files, data is accessible through the file system and directly through S3 APIs at the same time. AWS says thousands of compute resources can connect to the same S3 file system simultaneously, enabling shared access across clusters without duplicating data. S3 Files works with all the existing data in S3 buckets, with no migration required. It caches actively used data for low-latency access and provides up to multiple terabytes per second of aggregate read throughput. Some third-party suppliers offer similar capabilities.     "content": "AWS Engineer Reports PostgreSQL Performance Halved By Linux 7.0, But A Fix May Not Be Easy - Phoronix Articles & Reviews News Archive Forums Premium Ad-Free Contact Popular Categories Close Articles & Reviews News Archive Forums Premium Contact Categories Computers Display Drivers Graphics Cards Linux Gaming Memory Motherboards Processors Software Storage Operating Systems Peripherals AWS Engineer Reports PostgreSQL Performance Halved By Linux 7.0, But A Fix May Not Be Easy Written by Michael Larabel in Linux Kernel on 4 April 2026 at 07:36 AM EDT. 99 Comments An Amazon/AWS engineer raised the alarms on Friday over the current Linux 7.0 development kernel leading to the throughput for the PostgreSQL database server being around half that of prior kernel versions. The culprit halving the PostgreSQL performance is known but a revert looks like it may not happen and currently suggesting that PostgreSQL may need to be adapted. Salvatore Dipietro of Amazon/AWS reported a throughput and latency regression for PostgreSQL. They found Linux 7.0 in its near-final form delivering around 0.51x the throughputof prior kernels on a Graviton4 server due to now much more time being spent in a user-space spinlock. Bisecting the regression was traced back to the Linux 7.0 change of restricting the available preemption modes for the kernel. That change was previously covered on Phoronix within Linux 7.0 To Focus Just On Full & Lazy Preemption Models For Up-To-Date CPU Archs and in turn upstreamed with the Linux 7.0 scheduler updates . As a result, yesterday posted to the Linux kernel mailing list was a patch to restore PREEMPT_NONE as the default given the severity of the reported regression. While fixing an active performance regression, it looks like this change to restore PREEMPT_NONE as the default preemption model might not be picked up. Peter Zijlstra who authored the original code simplifying the preemption modes has responded that the \"fix\" is to make PostgreSQL make use of the Restartable Sequences (RSEQ) time slice extension. That time slice extension support was also upstreamed for Linux 7.0. \"The fix here is to make PostgreSQL make use of rseq slice extension: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/ [email protected] That should limit the exposure to lock holder preemption (unless PostgreSQL is doing seriously egregious things).\" So if that stands and shifting the blame to PostgreSQL, Linux 7.0 stable could lead to a significant drop for PostgreSQL performance in some scenarios until that popular database server is updated. Linux 7.0 stable is due out in about two weeks. This is also the kernel version powering Ubuntu 26.04 LTS to be released later in April. 99 Comments Tweet Related News Linux's Second-In-Command Turns To New Fuzzing Tools For Uncovering Kernel Bugs Linux 7.0-rc7 Released With Improved Docs For AI Agents, WiFi Driver Performance Fix Linux 7.1 Expected To Begin Removing i486 CPU Support Meta Has A New Linux Optimization To Avoid Throttling TCP Throughput Unnecessarily Snapdragon X2's Adreno X2-85 GPU Sees Driver Improvements For Linux 7.1 April 1 Linux Patches: Verified Birth Date For File Creation, Block Emacs From Running"

Most cloud security incidents stem from customer-side issues such as identity misuse, misconfigurations, and exposed workloads. Effective security for AWS cloud requires least-privilege IAM, encryption by default, continuous vulnerability management, and secure container practices. With the AWS shared responsibility model placing identity, configuration, and workload protection squarely on customers, misconfigurations and permission creep now drive most incidents. Unified visibility across identities, configurations, workloads, and compliance improves prioritization and reduces real-world risk. What Securing the AWS Cloud Really Means in 2026 Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud security is the discipline of protecting cloud infrastructure, data, applications, and workloads on AWS through a combination of architectural choices, native controls, and continuous independent assurance. In 2026, this definition has materially evolved. Cloud environments are no longer static collections of servers and networks. They are fluid systems defined by code, composed of ephemeral workloads, and exposed through APIs. Attackers have adapted accordingly. Most breaches now originate from identity misuse, configuration drift, and exposed services rather than flaws in underlying infrastructure. As a result, the cloud security for AWS must shift from periodic validation to real-time governance, emphasizing risk-driven insights over blanket control compliance. AWS is accountable for securing the cloud itself. This includes physical facilities, hardware, networking, and the virtualization layer. Customers are accountable for everything built on top of that foundation, including operating systems, network exposure, identities, access policies, applications, data, and compliance controls. More than a decade ago, as an AWS trainer, I spent countless hours explaining the fundamental differences between object storage and file systems. My favorite analogy was comparing S3 objects to books in a library (you can\u2019t edit a page, you need to replace the whole book) versus files on your computer that you can modify page by page. I drew diagrams, created metaphors, and helped customers understand why they needed different storage types for different workloads. Well, today that distinction becomes a bit more flexible. With S3 Files, Amazon S3 is the first and only cloud object store that offers fully-featured, high-performance file system access to your data. It makes your buckets accessible as file systems. This means changes to data on the file system are automatically reflected in the S3 bucket and you have fine-grained control over synchronization. S3 Files can be attached to multiple compute resources enabling data sharing across clusters without duplication. Until now, you had to choose between Amazon S3 cost, durability, and the services that can natively consume data from it or a file system\u2019s interactive capabilities. S3 Files eliminates that tradeoff. S3 becomes the central hub for all your organization\u2019s data. It\u2019s accessible directly from any AWS compute instance, container, or function, whether you\u2019re running production applications, training ML models, or building agentic AI systems. You can access any general purpose bucket as a native file system on your Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances, containers running on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) or Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) , or AWS Lambda functions. The file system presents S3 objects as files and directories, supporting all Network File System (NFS) v4.1+ operations like creating, reading, updating, and deleting files. As you work with specific files and directories through the file system, associated file metadata and contents are placed onto the file system\u2019s high-performance storage. By default, files that benefit from low-latency access are stored and served from the high performance storage. For files not stored on high performance storage such as those needing large sequential reads, S3 Files automatically serves those files directly from Amazon S3 to maximize throughput. For byte-range reads, only the requested bytes are transferred, minimizing data movement and costs. The system also supports intelligent pre-fetching to anticipate your data access needs. You have fine-grained control over what gets stored on the file"
